No entries dropped for wrong price or date: all Gowans figures matched the API. Researcher's PriceCharting entries kept as ASKING-style guides; Cool Spot added after the spine was read.
lots.guide_summary: Lot-level evidence is all SOLD at Gowans: four close boxed-Sega bundles at $50 to $110 hammer (4 to about 8 games) plus a mixed box at $80. No unsold. PriceCharting guides per title (ASKING-style averages, USD at an assumed 1.50, not checked live) sum to about A$91 if all seven are loose and about A$227 if all are complete with manuals; these cases probably hold carts but manuals are unknown, so the true figure sits between and is optimistic for a Tasmanian auction.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close boxed SOLD comparable is $55 (lot 389146, 5 boxed games, Feb 2026). 55 / 1.198 = 45.9, round down to $45. The $50 lot was excluded from the floor because 3 of its 4 games were loose carts. Flip: likely resale about $110 (Gowans 432091 box of about 8 boxed games, Aug 2026, consistent with the PriceCharting loose-to-complete span). Less 15% selling fee (assumed auction vendor commission, no outbound postage as a local resale) = 93.50. 93.50 / 2.396 = 39.0, round down to $35. Pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: All spines read and four close SOLD comparables opened with photos viewed, but none is the same set of titles and the contents of the cases (carts, manuals) are unseen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Do all seven cases contain the matching cartridge, and which have manuals? Is the Lotus II cart the US Genesis version, and is the QuackShot case or cart damaged beyond the stained spine?

lots.what_it_is: Modern reproduction two-seat cast metal garden bench in dark green, pierced foliage and bird back with an oval medallion of a seated woman, pierced scroll seat, scroll arms with ball finials, hoof feet. Gowans calls it CAST IRON BENCH SEAT; the metal (iron or aluminium) is not confirmed, as this design is widely made in cast aluminium.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo. No foundry mark or maker's name visible. Paint looks even and recent, with no obvious rust, cracks or missing pieces from the front. Side-by-side with Gowans lot 422189 (auction 351, July 2026, passed in) it is the identical design and colour, very likely the same bench being re-offered.
lots.condition: Looks sound and fully painted from the front; underside, joints, rust and metal type not assessed. Size not given.

lots.what_it_is: Framed modern colour facsimile after John Gould and H.C. Richter, Thylacinus cynocephalus (two thylacines standing on grass), from Mammals of Australia, in a gilt moulded frame with a dark brown mount. Decorative reproduction, not an original hand-coloured lithograph.
lots.key_photo_findings: Caption read on enlargement: 'H.C. Richter del. et lith.' at left, 'THYLACINUS CYNOCEPHALUS.' centred, 'Mintern Bros. Imp.' style printer line at right. There is no second 'Tasmanian Tiger' caption line, which matches Gowans lot 426030 (same printing) rather than the 'Tasmanian Tiger C1863' run. Flat even colour and a bright white sheet point to a modern print. Reflections in the glass hide the surface. This is the only two-animal Gould print in auction 366; four other thylacine prints in the sale are different plates.
lots.condition: Looks clean with no visible foxing through the glass; frame sound from the front. Surface, fading and the back not assessed.
